title: Here and now
grammar: Present Continuous, contrast with Present Simple

sections.heading: What is the Present Continuous?
sections.body: The Present Continuous is used to talk about actions happening right now, at this moment. It is also used for temporary situations and future arrangements.

sections.heading: Spelling rules for -ing
list: Most verbs add -ing: work → working, play → playing
Verbs ending in -e drop the -e: write → writing, make → making
Short verbs ending in consonant-vowel-consonant double the last letter: run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming

sections.heading: Negative
list: I am not sleeping.
She is not working today.
They are not listening.

sections.heading: Questions
sections.body: Put am / is / are before the subject.
list: Are you studying?
Is he working?
What are they doing?

sections.heading: Time expressions
list: now, right now, at the moment
today, this week, this morning (temporary)
Look! Listen! (to introduce something happening now)

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not forget the verb 'to be': 'I working' is wrong. Say 'I am working'.
Do not use Present Continuous for habits: 'I am usually getting up at 7' is wrong.
Remember the spelling rules for -ing.

list.definition: He is wearing a blue shirt.
I am wearing a white T-shirt.
I am wearing my new jeans.
She is wearing a red dress.
My sister is wearing a long skirt.
He is wearing a warm jacket.
I am wearing my winter coat.
She is wearing a summer hat.
The dog is running in the park.
My father is reading a newspaper.
The students are writing a test.
We are talking on the phone.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I am reading a book right now.
She is wearing a red dress today.
They are playing football at the moment.
I usually drink coffee, but today I am drinking tea.
He is not working this week.
questions: In sentences 1, 2 and 3, which structure do we use to describe actions happening now?
In sentence 4, why do we use Present Continuous after 'Look!'?
In sentence 5, why are two different tenses used in the same sentence?
In sentence 6, how do we make the negative?
In sentences 7 and 8, how do we make questions?

questions.explanation: For actions happening now we use Present Continuous: is + verb-ing.
With 'you' we use 'Are' in Present Continuous questions.

questions.prompt: I usually ___ coffee, but today I ___ tea.
questions.explanation: Usually goes with Present Simple, today with Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: She ___ a book at the moment.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Look around you and write 5 sentences about what people are doing right now.
Write 5 sentences about what your family members are doing at this moment.
Compare your usual routine with what you are doing today. Write 5 sentences using 'usually' and 'today'.

questions.prompt: She ___ her homework at the moment.
We usually ___ to school, but today we ___ the bus.
questions.explanation: Usually = Present Simple, today = Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: He ___ wearing a blue shirt today.
I ___ reading a very good book this week.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Present Continuous: am / is / are + verb-ing.
Use it for actions happening now, temporary situations and future arrangements.
Negative: add 'not' after am / is / are.
Questions: put am / is / are before the subject.
Spelling: drop -e (write → writing), double consonant (run → running).

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Forgetting 'to be': 'I working' is wrong. Say 'I am working'.
Using Present Continuous for habits: 'I am usually waking up at 7' is wrong.
Forgetting the -ing form.

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: I am ... -ing right now.
She is ... -ing at the moment.
Look! ... is ... -ing.
Listen! ... is ... -ing.
What are you doing?
I usually ..., but today I am ...
